fact: L'Union reports the 196 km Fougamou-Mouila section (Ngounie province), built and pre-financed by Moov Africa Gabon Telecom, now connects Fougamou and Mouila to the national backbone; it is the first segment of phase 1 of the extension, ceded to the State by a convention signed at Mouila (dated 'yesterday' in a 7 Oct 2026 article).
GabonReview reports the national backbone in operation at 1,782 km of fibre, with a state official citing about 2,000 km today; places not listed.

GabonReview reports SPIN signed a 20-year concession with Gabon Fiber S.A. on 14 Sep 2026 under which Gabon Fiber will finance and build 1,651 km more (over 41 billion CFA francs), in three phases starting with Lambarene-Mouila-Tchibanga and Lalara-Makokou-Okondja, taking the network from 1,782 to 3,433 km.
GabonReview reports Gabon Fiber, concessionaire of the backbone, will operate exclusively on the wholesale market and not compete with telecom operators and ISPs; it will market capacity.

GabonReview reports the existing national backbone at 1,769 km, owned by SPIN and operated until the delegation to Bouygues Energies & Services-Axione expired on 15 Nov 2026 (as stated); places not listed.

GabonReview reports the SPIN-Gabon Fiber contract signed 14 Sep 2026 has Gabon Fiber finance and build 1,651 km additional fibre, taking the network to about 3,420 km, under a 20-year lease-concession from 16 Nov 2026.
GabonReview reports the contract imposes 'open and non-discriminatory' access for operators on the backbone, with performance and cybersecurity obligations.
Agence Gabonaise de Presse reports about 1,800 km of existing backbone network, owned outright by SPIN; places not listed.

AGP reports a 20-year public-private partnership signed 14 Sep 2026 under which Gabon Fiber S.A. designs, finances, builds and operates about 1,700 km of extension, to reach about 3,500 km, privately financed.
Tech Africa News reports 1,769 km of existing national backbone network, described as strategic infrastructure transporting electronic communications across Gabon; places not listed.

Gabonclic reports the national fibre backbone, run by Axione Gabon along the railway line, carried internet, mobile and fixed telephony in the Ogooue-Ivindo, Woleu-Ntem, Ogooue-Lolo and Haut-Ogooue provinces until it was cut at PK 289 in the Lope on 24 August 2026 (about 09:40); partial outage, repairs under way on 25 August.

SPIN states the 196 km Lambarene-Mouila fibre section, first segment of phase 1 of the national backbone extension, was commissioned on 6 October 2026, connecting Fougamou and Mouila to the national network.

Gabon Fiber S.A. signed concessions with the state infrastructure holding SPIN on 2026-09-14 to build about 1,650 km of additional fibre extending the Backbone National Gabonais to Lambarene, Makokou, Ovan, Mouila, Ndende, Lebamba, Okondja, Ngouoni, Tchibanga and Mayumba; the AGP report says the company still intends to raise over FCFA 41bn on international markets.
Seminar participants (SPIN, Ageos, Aninf, ministry) said Gabon will build on 2,000 km of optical fibre already deployed; no places, regions or lit status are given.
The same report says extension works on the national fibre are under way; no contract, route or contractor is given.

SPIN states that the Backbone National Gabonais fibre optic network supports the Wi-Fi hotspots put into service 9-11 December 2024 in schools at Bakoumba, Bongoville and Léconi (Haut-Ogooué) and Oyem (Woleu-Ntem).
L'Union reports that in January 2017 ANINF sent agents to Franceville to check it was interconnected to the Gabonese national backbone network, as it had done at Mouila and Oyem in 2015.
